summary: Beatrice Erskine Lane Suzuki worked in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Radcliffe College (~1894–1898) under William James, Josiah Royce, and George Santayana, and later attended Columbia University (~1907–1909).

Ben Jiao specializes in Tibetology. He completed his Ph.D. at Case Western Reserve University under Melvyn C. Goldstein in 2001, and served as Deputy Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Research Institute at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2008).
Ben Joffe works in Tibetology and religious studies. He completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Colorado Boulder under the supervision of Carole McGranahan.

Benedetta Lomi works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from SOAS University of London, taught at the University of Virginia (~2013–2017), and held a post at the University of Bristol (~2017).

Benimadhab Barua was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. Educated at Chittagong College, Krishnagar Government College, Krishnath College, the University of Calcutta, and the University of London, he served at the University of Calcutta from 1918 to 1948.

Benjamin A. Elman is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. After studying at Hamilton College, American University, and the University of Pennsylvania, he served as Professor at UCLA (attested 2004) and East Asian Studies Program Director at Princeton University (~2005–2012).
Benjamin Bogin specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan, studying under Donald S. Lopez Jr., Janet Gyatso, and Gareth Sparham.

Benjamin Brose works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his Ph.D. at Stanford University (~2004–2010) under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, and served as assistant professor of Chinese Buddhism at the University of Michigan (~2010–2016).

Benjamin Wood specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Toronto under Frances Garrett, having also studied under Khenpo Kunga Sherab, Shayne Clarke, and Thupten Champa.

Benkyo Shiio was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1900–1903). He held posts at Waseda University, Taisho University (~1926–1944), and served as head of the Sanko Library (~1960–1968).

Benoît Vermander works in Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy, having studied at Yale, Paris Institute of Political Studies, Fu Jen Catholic University, and Facultés Loyola Paris. He was Academic Director at Taipei Ricci Institute (1996–2009) and joined Fudan University in 2009.

Bernard Faure specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology, earning doctorates from Paris Diderot and the University of Paris. He taught at Cornell University (~1983–1987), Stanford University (~1987–2006), and Columbia University as Kao Professor (~2006).

Bernard Frank was a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. He served as head of the Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1979–1982) and held the chair of Civilisation japonaise at Collège de France (1979–1996).

Bernhard Geiger was an Indology, Iranian, and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Vienna (~1899–1904). He held posts at Vienna (~1909–1938), the Tibetan-Iranian Institute (1938–1951), and Columbia University (~1947–1951).
Bernhard Hirzel was an Indologist who studied at the University of Göttingen and under Franz Bopp (~1830–1833). He served as a Dozent at the University of Zurich from ~1835 to 1839.

Bernhard Kölver was an Indology scholar who served at the University of Cologne (1966–1970), the Nepal Research Centre (~1970–1972), the University of Kiel as Professor (1977–1993), and Leipzig University (1993–2001).

Bernie Glassman was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies who studied at NYU Tandon School of Engineering and trained under Taizan Maezumi (~1970–1995). He founded Zen Peacemakers (attested 2002).

Berthe Jansen works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After degrees at Leiden and Oxford, she earned her PhD at Leiden under Jonathan A. Silk (~2009–2015), later serving as a fellow at Heidelberg (~2015) and visiting professor at Leiden (2015–2016).

Berthold Delbrück was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Halle-Wittenberg and Berlin under August Friedrich Pott and Albrecht Weber. He held a post at Halle-Wittenberg (1867) and the Sanskrit and comparative linguistics chair at Jena (1870–1913).

Berthold Laufer studied Sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies at Berlin and Leipzig under August Conrady, Georg von der Gabelentz, and Wilhelm Grube. He held posts at Columbia University (~1905–1907) and the Field Museum (~1908–1934).
